text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected on /v1/stream (p99 latency 3.2s > 2.0s SLO). Auto-page to oncall.
Alice C.: seeing lots of failed streams from customers, p99 tail is through the roof. kicking off thread to triage.
Raj P.: looking at dashboards now — spike starts ~1794799800, p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~3.2s, error rate up ~0.6%.
Sam R. (SRE): any rollout around that time? deploy-bot shows a merge ~1794799700 in infra/preproc (PR #614).
Kevin L. (ML Infra): that PR touched prompt-template expansion and added heavy JSON schema validation in preproc. I flagged it in review but it passed.
Maya S. (Support): customer impact: 4 enterprise tenants reported streaming stalls and truncated responses. One reported generator hung mid-output.
Alice C.: streaming stalls match where we do prompt assembly + tokenizer run. hypothesis: template expansion + JSON mode validation added CPU/latency per request.
Raj P.: confirmed higher CPU in preproc pods at the spike window. CPU per-request median increased ~18%.
Sam R. (SRE): tail samples from request logs show long blocking on `preproc::assemble_prompt()` ~1.5s in worst cases.
Kevin L. (ML Infra): looks like certain prompts with tool schemas trigger the new validator path which does deep recursion on nested inputs. That's O(n^2) in pathological templates.
Alice C.: mitigation options: 1) rollback PR 614 (fast) 2) enable feature-flag to disable validator (fast) 3) route live traffic to compatible fallback model variant (safer) 4) increase preproc autoscale and CPU (works but costly).
Jordan (oncall): I'm taking over the page. Starting immediate mitigation.
Sam R. (SRE): I'm going to flip the feature flag `preproc.disable_schema_validation=true` on the staging ring to measure effect.
Raj P.: copying current query sample — truncated: `{"prompt_template": "{user_input} \ntools: {tools_schema}", "tools_schema": {...deep nested...}}`
Kevin L. (ML Infra): enabling the flag should bypass the heavy recursion. I can flip in prod if tests look good.
Sam R. (SRE): flipped in staging, p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.4s on staging traffic. Good signal.
Alice C.: plan: flip flag in prod canary (10% traffic) -> monitor p95/p99 and error rate -> full flip if stable. Also alert customers and open follow-up for safer validator rewrite.
Jordan (oncall): executing prod canary now. Command: `./ops/flagset --env=prod --flag=preproc.disable_schema_validation --value=true --pct=10`
Ops Bot: command received, applying to 10% prod traffic.
Sam R. (SRE): canary applied. monitoring streams.
Raj P.: immediate p99 for canary cohort down to ~1.3s. overall prod p99 trending down but still elevated due to other rings.
Maya S. (Support): informing affected customers: "We are aware of streaming degradation, currently routing mitigating traffic and expect improvement within 15-30m. Will post updates."
Alice C.: also enabling `json_bypass_mode` for streaming endpoints for enterprise tenants who use large tool schemas — this reduces prompt templating and sends structured payload directly to model.
Kevin L. (ML Infra): `json_bypass_mode` reduces preproc work but may change safety invariants; limit to tenant opt-in for now.
Jordan (oncall): will we need to roll back PR 614 after this?
Kevin L. (ML Infra): we should revert or patch. Short term: revert PR 614, long term: implement iterative validator (streaming-friendly) + performance tests.
Sam R. (SRE): initiating rollback of PR 614 now: `git revert -m 1 <commit>` then deploy.
Ops Bot: rollback pipeline started for infra/preproc.
Alice C.: Jordan, handoff note: if p99 < 2.0s and error rate <0.3% for 30m post-rollback, we can close page and open postmortem.
Jordan (oncall): acknowledged. I'll run post-incident customer impact table and coordinate SLA credits if necessary.
Raj P.: quick note — streaming stalls correlated with requests that include large `tools_schema` arrays (>50 items) and `json_mode: true`. Those trigger deep validation loops.
Kevin L. (ML Infra): add a soft limit on `tools_schema` size: reject >100 items or stream validation. I'll open PR to add early cutoff with monitoring metric `preproc.schema_depth_exceeded`.
Maya S. (Support): creating incident email template for customers: short description, mitigation steps, expected ETA, and point of contact.
Sam R. (SRE): rollback deployed to all rings at 1794801200. Observed global p99 drop to 1.2s within 3m. error rate back to baseline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SLO restored (p99 1.2s). Incident severity downgraded to SEV3.
Alice C.: great. root cause summary: PR #614 introduced an eager schema validator in preproc that is expensive for nested tool schemas and certain prompt templates, causing preproc CPU spike and streaming tail latency.
Jordan (oncall): I'm taking postmortem lead. Assigning action items: 1) Kevin — rewrite validator to be streaming-friendly + add perf tests (ETA 2 weeks). 2) DevEx — add size limits and warning when template expansion > 2k chars. 3) SRE (Sam) — add alert for `preproc.schema_depth_exceeded` and preproc CPU tail > 85% (ETA 3 days). 4) Support (Maya) — notify impacted customers and draft SLA credit proposal (ETA 24h).
Kevin L. (ML Infra): ack. Also adding canary tests for schema-heavy requests.
Sam R. (SRE): handoff complete to Jordan. I'll stay on for 15m to ensure stability.
Jordan (oncall): thanks team. Closing page in 30m if metrics stay green. Logging timeline for postmortem.
Maya S. (Support): CC'd customers updated.
Alice C.: follow-up: run a sweep to find other code paths that do deep recursion during prompt assembly (e.g., tool schema expansion in JSON mode, `format_tool_help()` helpers).
Raj P.: saved key log snippets to `s3://redwood-incident-logs/1794800001/` and added sample bad payloads for infra.
Kevin L. (ML Infra): adding unit that simulates 100 concurrent `tools_schema` items to avoid regressions.
Jordan (oncall): final status at 1794802400: p99 1.2s, error rate baseline, rollback completed, feature-flag off for prod, customers notified. Turning incident into postmortem.
Alice C.: :white_check_mark: good work everyone.
